additionalCoursework: Enrollment in any of the additional Science courses may be beneficial to applicants: comparative vertebrate anatomy, computer science, embryology, histology, microbiology, molecular genetics, physiology.  Selections from the following arts and humanities courses is recommended: English, ethics, foreign languages, history, philosophy, psychology, public speaking, sociology.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: Members of groups underrepresented in medicine are encouraged to apply. The School of Medicine's Office of Community and  Health Education actively recruits students from groups underrepresented in medicine and provides counseling for high school and college students. Further information may be obtained by contacting Dr. Robert Maupin, Associate Dean for Community and Health Education, at 504 568 8501.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence:
A leave of absence for a short period of several weeks up to one year may be granted to a student in good standing, subject to the discretion of the Dean, because of illness or other appropriate reasons. Students taking short-term leaves of absence of less than one week must make acceptable arrangements with the faculty involved for completion of course work and other assignments which will be missed. Leave of absence of a longer duration may be granted students in good standing for reasons of a personal nature or to participate in a special program of research or other activity designed to augment the student's academic training. Specific arrangements must be made on an individual basis with the Dean before beginning a leave of absence. The University policy governing the processing of leave of absence are applicable and is described in the general information section of this publication.

medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: There are several organizations that students may join according to their interests.  Students are encouraged to participate in Community Outreach opportunities and can receive credit for doing so.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: LSU School of Medicine is located in downtown New Orleans in a medical corridor which is within walking distance of the historic French Quarter, museums, shopping districts, and two sports arenas for professional football and basketball teams.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Furnished and unfurnished apartments are available for married s are available(with or without children) and single students. Many students choose to rent apartments in New Orleans or the surrounding metropolitan area.  Lists of available apartments are supplied upon request.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Safe Space Training for faculty and staff and trained individuals have markers identifying their offices as resources for student’s to connect. Additionally the Tiger Pride Student/Campus Association chapter services as an organized resource

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Faculty are readily available to serve the needs of our students including the LSUHSC Mentors Program.  Tutors are also available for medical students during the first two years of coursework.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Varied: small groups, lectures, simulation labs and clinical rotations
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Some sessions are mandatory,  The student is advised when class is mandatory.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: Curriculum renewal at the LSU School of Medicine is an ongoing process.  Currently, the first two years of the medical school curriculum emphasize several basic sciences and their relevance to clinical medicine. Clinical experiences begin in the first year in courses such as the Science and Practice of Medicine. The second year of medical school utilizes an integrated approach to the teaching of basic science and pre-clinical courses within an environment that fosters an early exposure to patient care. Clerkships begin in the third year, where students rotate through the various clinical disciplines. In the fourth year, students are given several months for electives in addition to required rotations in Ambulatory Medicine, Acting Internships, etc. Some of these rotations can be completed at institutions associated with the LSU School of Medicine throughout the state or at other approved institutions outside the state or country. medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: We currently have a 4-year rural track designed to educate students interested in becoming a primary-care physician in a rural setting.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Many faculty welcome students to work in their laboratories.  In addition to our MD/PhD program, the Medical School also has an Honor's Program in which students can conduct research.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: University Hospital, Veterans Administration Hospital, Children's Hospital, Touro.  Hospitals in Lafayette and Baton Rouge
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Honors, High Pass, Pass and Fail

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: LSU School of Medicine in New Orleans was established in 1931 in downtown New Orleans. During the past two decades, several new buildings have been erected, including a state-of-the-art Student Learning Center which includes procedural and simulation labs, a computer lounge, and large and small-group meeting rooms. A new residence facility, Stanislaus Hall, containing a comprehensive fitness center, is among the more recent additions to the campus.  A new 425-bed, state-of-the-art teaching hospital is now open and a new Veterans' Administration hospital which contains over 200 beds opened in late 2016. As part of this medical corridor, a new building, the Louisiana Cancer Research Consortium has already opened.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: The LSU School of Medicine is dedicated to providing the opportunity for an excellent medical education to all  applicants who are prepared to benefit from its curriculum and instruction. To this end, the Admissions Committee will strive to recruit and admit residents from Louisiana from every geographic, economic, social, and cultural dimension of the state of Louisiana and also other states within the country.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: Applicants may include additional letters from research or employers, but must meet the requirement in order be considered.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: Composite recommendations from pre-professional committees or 3 letters from professors who have taught the applicant in the sciences or math in didactic classes.  Letters from laboratory or research professors are not acceptable.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Information is given to those who are invited to interview two weeks prior to appointment.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Three one-on-one interviews.  Interviews will be through a virtual platform.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: All interviews will be conducted via a virtual platform.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: All residents of the State of Louisiana, out-of-state applicants are pre-screened.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: All out of state applicants will be pre-screened.  Those applicants chosen to move to the next step will receive a secondary application.  .
medSchoolApplication.acceptCanadianApplInformation: Canadian applicants are considered in the same group as out of state applicants.  Canadian applicant are pre-screened.  Those chosen to move to the next step will receive a secondary application.
medSchoolApplication.acceptInternationalApplInformation: Students have to have attended a North American College or University and have  Permanent Resident Status in the United States.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: LSU New Orleans considers the most recent MCAT score for admissions.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: LSUHSC-New Orleans will substitute Thirty Hours or greater of Post Bac or Graduate  Science coursework for the applicant's undergraduate GPA.  There is no minimum GPA
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: LSUHSC-New Orleans has a 30 hour policy; whereas, 30 hours of upper level science courswork will be substituted for undergraduate GPA.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: While credits from a 4 year institution is preferably.  Applicants may still apply with credits from community colleges.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Please send any letters of intent, interest or updates to ms-admissions@lsuhsc.edu.  If you are applying as an Out of State applicant you may send us a letter discussing your ties to Louisiana.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Financial assistance is available for students through several different methods. There are direct scholarship programs, scholarships for disadvantaged students, state and federal loan programs, work-study programs, and employment opportunities in the New Orleans area for students in their third and fourth years. Financial assistance information is available from the Student Financial Aid Office at 504 568 4820.

medSchoolPrograms.programLength: The 4 year Dual Degree Program integrates curricula in the School of Medicine and School of Public Health to prepare medical students as excellent clinicians who can improve the health communities through application of knowledge and skills from on of the five public health disciplines.
medSchoolPrograms.deadline: Applicants may on their primary ro secondary applications.  Student have to first be accepted into medical school before they can be accepted into the Master's program.

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: In accordance with the AAMC policies, LSU SOM New Orleans will ask that accepted students  to use choose your medical school tool and plan to enroll to LSU on or prior to April 30th.

All applicants holding an acceptance offer at LSU New Orleans should commit to enroll no later than July 1st,  prior to orientation.  At that time the applicant has withdrawn from all other medical schools

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Applicants are notified that they are placed on the waitlist.   Being accepted off of the waitlist varies every year.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: Applicants are required to have 38 hours of science as shown in the Recommended Premedical Coursework shown below.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: Pre-Requisite coursework older than 5 years should be followed by a satisfactory completion of upper level science coursework.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Candidates are encouraged to contact the Office of Admissions (MS-Admissions@lsuhsc.edu) for a brochure which summarizes the criteria for selection to the LSU School of Medicine in New Orleans. Children of alumni of this School of Medicine who no longer reside in Louisiana and/or applicants to the combined MD/PhD program are also eligible for acceptance. Consideration is also given to a percentage of non-residents.  Applicants accepted from these latter categories will be responsible for paying out-of-state tuition for the duration of their enrollment. Matriculants in the most recent entering class represented 60 undergraduate institutions.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Applicants should have a variety clinical experiences.   Shadowing is just recommended.  Applicants should seek clinical experiences where they will have the most opportunity for exposure to the practice of medicine.
